Plus, you really shouldn't be packing on the bf% while bulking, not anymore than a few %.

As a natural lifter (which I assume you are) unless you have just started lifting, an excessive bulk is going to simply result in you putting on pure fat with maybe a little muscle. My first clean bulk at 3500 calories was difficult to say the least. I used a blender in order to make a 1000 calorie mid afternoon... i hesitate to call it a shake, more of a puree, which was a combination of Tuna, mixed nuts, olive oil raw eggs, cucumber and tomato, in those 5 months of clean bulking I put on about 11kg (24lbs), I then dropped 4kg (9lbs) over 3 months through a very minor calorie deficit of 250 a day in order to preserve as much muscle mass as possible. If i tried to repeat these results almost all the weight I would gain would be fat, would I gain some muscle? sure, but not a lot. And I lift 6 times a week relying on pure linear progression in the 4-6 rep range as a new lifter then switching to a combination of this with Western Periodization for the lifts I had plateaued in with a deload every 8-12 weeks. Yes its important to consume more calories than you burn in order to be in a fed state and build muscle, but unless you decide to start shooting anabolics into your glutes you're capacity for building muscle is going to be very slow. So you may as well slow bulk by using a food diary to dial in your optimal building calories while tolerating minimal adipose tissue during the process.
